steps.body: Partial quotients removes groups in whatever chunks are convenient, then adds the chunks up. 852 ÷ 4 can take 200 fours, then 13 more.
steps.narration: Partial quotients removes groups in whatever chunks are convenient, then adds the chunks up. 852 ÷ 4 can take 200 fours, then 13 more.

widget.prompt: 852 ÷ 4 — slide to the quotient the chunks must total.
widget.lowFeedback: Too low — 200 fours alone already account for 800 of the 852.
widget.highFeedback: Too high — more than 213 fours would overshoot 852 entirely.
widget.successFeedback: 213 — reachable as 200 fours then 13 more, or any chunks totalling the same.

predict.prompt: Taking 200 fours out of 852 first, is that legal?
predict.reveal: 800 fits inside 852, so the chunk is legal — and it does most of the work in a single step.

cml.actionGoal: Split a factor into places, build each piece, and reassemble the whole for g4m partial quotient.
invariants: Splitting a factor never changes the product: every piece of the split multiplies the other factor, and the pieces add back to exactly the same total, which is what makes g4m partial quotient decomposable at all.
misconceptions: Adding only some of the partial products, dropping or inventing a zero when factors carry tens, or letting a remainder reach or exceed the divisor.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one partial product were left out, exactly how much of the total would go missing?

widget.prompt: Finding successive chunks in 852 ÷ 4, a student takes 200 fours first. Why is that allowed?

options.label: Because any number of groups can be removed at once, in any order
options.feedback: Correct — partial quotients removes convenient chunks and adds them up; the order never changes the total.

options.label: Because 200 is the only correct first chunk
options.feedback: It is convenient, not required — 100 fours twice reaches the same place, just more slowly.

options.label: Because 4 × 200 is bigger than 852
options.feedback: 4 × 200 is 800, which fits inside 852 — that is exactly why the chunk is legal.

options.label: It is not allowed — you must take one group at a time
options.feedback: Taking one at a time works but is enormously slow; chunking is the whole point of the method.
